7.text: More frequently, however, agreements like this are concluded between

8.text: friendly families on the basis of the exchange of one woman for another.

9.text: Marriage between Persons of Disproportionate Ages. — The age of

10.text: women thus exchanged is hardly considered at all. For instance, on the Oloi

11.text: River, a man named Qɪˊmɪqäi married his young son five years old to a girl

22.text: I was told of a boy of two, who was still being nursed, and who had

23.text: lost his mother. She had died of influenza. Since the family wanted a woman

24.text: worker, the infant boy was almost immediately married to a full-grown girl.

25.text: In due time the bride bore a child from a marriage-companion. When she

26.text: was nursing her own child, she also nursed her infant husband. Chukchee

27.text: boys often are nursed until five or six years old. In this case the husband

28.text: also readily took the breast of his wife. When I asked for the reason of

29.text: the woman’s conduct, the Chukchee replied, “Who knows? Perhaps it is a

30.text: kind of incantation to insure the love of the young husband in the future.”⁴
